title: Private Tours & Exclusive Family Experiences in Asia: Behind Closed Doors
excerpt: After-hours access to Angkor Wat, private sushi masterclasses in Tokyo, helicopter tours over Hong Kong — the experiences that money can buy and memory can keep.
author: Family Travel Asia Team
content:
## Asia's Most Exclusive Family Experiences

The best luxury is privacy. Having a world-famous landmark to yourself, a private chef in your villa, or after-hours access to a temple. Here's the shortlist of experiences that money can buy and memory can keep.

### Angkor Wat at Dawn (Private Access)

"We entered Angkor Wat through a side gate before sunrise. No crowds. No selfie sticks. Just us, the temple, and the sound of birds waking up. My 10-year-old said it was 'better than a movie.'" — The Martins

**How:** Book through a specialist operator like Abercrombie & Kent or Remote Lands. They arrange after-hours permits. Cost: ~$1,500 for a family of 4 including guide.

**Pro tip:** Combine with a private Khmer cooking class afterward. The contrast between ancient temples and modern Cambodian kitchens is perfect for curious kids.

### Tokyo Private Sushi Masterclass

"A Jiro-inspired sushi master came to our hotel suite with fresh fish from Toyosu Market. My 8-year-old learned to make nigiri. The chef said she had 'natural hands.' She still talks about it." — The Yoshida family

**How:** Concierge at any top Tokyo hotel (Aman, Park Hyatt, Palace) can arrange this. Cost: ~$500-800 for a 2-hour private session.

**What you get:** Fresh fish selection, rice preparation lesson, nigiri and maki techniques, and a certificate signed by the chef.

### Hong Kong by Helicopter

"The helicopter tour over Hong Kong is the single best family experience we've ever done. The pilot pointed out our hotel from the air. My 6-year-old shouted 'that's our pool!' Best $2,000 we ever spent." — The Chans

**How:** Heliservices Hong Kong offers private charters. 15-minute city tour (~$500/person) or 30-minute extended tour including Lantau Island (~$900/person).

### Bangkok Private Longtail Boat + Floating Market

"We hired a private longtail boat for the day. The guide took us to a floating market before the tourist boats arrived. We ate coconut pancakes in peace while watching vendors paddle to us. Perfect." — Sarah, mom of two

**How:** Book through a local operator or hotel concierge. Cost: ~$300-500 for a full-day private boat with English-speaking guide.

### Bali Private Silver-Making Workshop

"A master silversmith in Ubud taught my 7-year-old to make a ring. She wore it every day for a year. The smith sent us photos of the process. $80 for a memory that lasted forever." — The Davises

**How:** Any villa concierge in Bali can arrange this. Or contact Studio Perak in Ubud directly. Cost: $50-100 per person including materials.

### Maldives Sandbank Dinner

"They set up a table on a sandbank. Candles. Lanterns. The staff arrived by boat with our dinner. We ate lobster while the sunset turned the Indian Ocean purple. Our kids collected shells. It was surreal." — Multiple honeymooning parents

**How:** Available at most luxury resorts (Soneva, Cheval Blanc, Waldorf Astoria). Cost: $300-500 per couple including kids' menu.

### The Ultimate: Private Jet Charter

"We chartered a jet from Singapore to Langkawi. 8 seats. Direct flight. No queues. The kids watched movies on the sofa while we had breakfast. It's not about the cost — it's about arriving fresh." — The tech CEO family

**How:** Companies like VistaJet and Fly Victor offer empty-leg deals for 50-70% off. Cost: $3,000-8,000 depending on route.

### Bottom Line

The best exclusive experiences in Asia are the ones where you have a personal guide, private access, and no crowds. Book through your hotel concierge or specialist operators. The cost is high but the memories are priceless. Angkor Wat at dawn is the one experience every family should do at least once.
